the_answer: NOT YET, and the remaining distance is three separable things, only one of which is about numerical accuracy. (1) **38.1862 %** of the model's gradient mass ALREADY agrees with upstream's own training step as well as an independent bf16 reimplementation could -- on the SHIPPED path, today. (2) A further **51.1358 %** gets there only with every softmax computed accurately, which is a measurement bound and not a shippable lever; on the shipped path that mass fails by 91.31x and the entire factor is the softmax. (3) **2.8431 %** (aux_heads) is VOID rather than measured -- its forward disagrees, so A18 invalidates any gradient statement about it. (4) **7.8349 %** has no direct reading, and that now includes the pairformer trunk: its reading was withdrawn at pass 175 because it scored our 0.4.3-convention port against a 0.5.0-convention reference (D90/D91).

the_bar: sqrt(2) x threshold (PROTOCOL A26). The 'equals float64' threshold is unreachable for any bf16 port: two independent error vectors of equal size subtract to sqrt(2) times one of them. Scoring a bf16 port against the unreachable threshold manufactures a failure, which the campaign did for 174 passes.
the_deepest_finding: every disagreement we measure is GEOMETRY, not an unexplained defect. With q = ||our error|| / ||their error|| and the cosine between the two error vectors, ||e-t||/||t|| = sqrt(q^2 + 1 - 2q cos) predicts all three measured scopes to within 1.26e-05, across a range spanning 129x. So 'do we reproduce training' reduces entirely to two measured quantities per scope. And it has a consequence that cost a row 35 % of its own error to demonstrate: past ||e|| ~ ||t||, getting MORE accurate does not get you closer to the reference -- bounding five more verbs in float64 removed 35 % of our error and bought 0.57 % of agreement.
the_question: do we reproduce OpenFold3 training on Tenstorrent? Measured as: does our training step's GRADIENT agree with the gradient upstream's own bf16 training step computes -- not with a float64 ideal neither side runs.
what: THE CAMPAIGN'S ANSWER, current as of pass 175. One place, superseding the scattered and partly-retracted artifacts listed under `supersedes`. Read this first.
what_changed_at_pass_175: I escalated the trunk's 46.67x as a PRODUCT DEFECT and withdrew it the same pass: reading the two upstream release trees showed 0.4.3 and 0.5.0 differ in the ending-node bias orientation, at the CALL SITE rather than the layer default, and our port implements the one matching our checkpoint. I then tried to confirm the magnitude by measurement and WITHDREW that too -- the estimate swings 0.81x / 135x / 3083x depending on weights and denominator, so it measures my choices. D90 stands on the source reading, which was never a magnitude argument.
what_changed_at_pass_176: Three things, and the third is the one to read. (1) The owed revision arm RAN (THE_REVISION_ARM_RAN.json): the transpose_bias orientation flag, measured on upstream's own two release trees with identical p2 weights on this same boundary, is worth 8.62x upstream's own bf16 on the pair track -- real and substantial, but it does NOT account for the 46.67x. Pre-registered branch B fired: REOPEN. The control read exactly 0.0. (2) D93/D94 read the revision diffs D22 never covered: msa_module is INERT so the campaign's positive result is safe, but aux_heads' two backing modules are NOT, and the trunk carries a SECOND difference -- 0.5.0 runs its trunk attention with use_high_precision_attention=True and 0.4.3 does not. (3) D95: relative L2 over a PADDED activation dilutes a structural difference 39x and bf16 noise only 1.2x, on this exact 56-real/384-padded boundary. That flips the qualitative verdict and it means A18 -- the rule that a disagreeing forward invalidates the gradient -- is nearly blind to the wrong-transform error it exists to catch.
what_is_now_less_certain_than_it_was: The GRADIENT headlines are parameter-space and D95 barely touches them; the percentages below stand. What weakens is the FORWARD evidence underneath them. Every A18 figure in this file was computed on a padded activation, so each pass is weaker evidence than stated and the aux_heads failure is less interpretable, not more. And the 7.8349 % with no direct reading -- which includes the trunk -- now has a MEASURED lower bound on how wrong scoring it against the wrong revision would be: 8.62x bf16 from one flag alone, with a second flag unquantified.

what_would_close_it.the_2_pct: 0.74055 % can never be read -- it sits on a weight the shipped path applies on the host, so no device gradient for it exists. The rest is the trunk's 240 unplaced fused-qkv leaves and small embedders.
what_would_close_it.the_51_pct: an accurate softmax in the diffusion transformer. Known, bounded, and release-gated: no shipped precision lever reaches the bar and the float64 bound costs 13 s per structure against 2.5 s.
what_would_close_it.the_8_pct: a port fix to the pairformer trunk's forward composition, and a diagnosis of aux_heads' plddt_logits forward. These are correctness bugs, not precision, and they are a different kind of work from everything else this campaign has done.
